# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:

  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1635
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1635
- **Title**: gh-1632 [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1632` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +59
- **Deletions**: -37
- **Created**: 2026-10-15T15:25:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-16T00:53:53Z

## PR Description

Refs #1632 (partial — the I1 default fix only; the goal card stays open). Not closing: core-tier AC5 (offline orphan-`tool_stuck` ledger REG + red-blocks-merge CI job, I4) and AC6 (fa version in session header, I5) are not implemented in this PR — they remain open on gh-1632 and must land before the card closes.
### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` on every non-headless host when no explicit `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine is intact — the fa 1.0.580 incident session simply ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits `tool_stuck` and never cancels/retries/converts: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then 27 minutes of heartbeats until the owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Violated invariant I1 (`advisory` = explicit opt-out only, never an implicit interactive default).

### Fix

# gh-1632: [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it

## Description

## Goal — stuck-call recovery that actually fires (v1)
One sentence: **a `tool_stuck` flag must always escalate — cancel → retry once → convert-to-background — so a hung tool call never outlives its own stuck threshold by more than the recovery budget; the model gets told and keeps working without a human poking the session.**

Observed failure (dmtools factory session `01a13fdc…`, 2026-10-15, fa **1.0.580**): a foreground `bash` call (work in `dmtools-agents`, incl. `git fetch` — network freeze or ssh/credential prompt with no tty) started 17:05:52Z, produced zero output. The liveness layer worked as documented — `tool_heartbeat` records every minute from 17:08:52, `tool_stuck` at **17:10:52** (= the 300 s floor, no declared timeout). Then **nothing**: the call sat hung for **27 minutes**. The `[liveness watchdog]` system notice reached the model only at **17:32:44** — 10 s after the OWNER's manual steering («как дела?», 17:32:34) soft-yielded the call to a background job. The agent then self-recovered in ~40 s (stopped the dead job, finished the task). gh-1054's supervision (heartbeats, stuck flag, autonomous cancel/retry/convert state machine in `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart`) either did not run in this build/mode or failed to fire — the goal is to make the escalation unconditional, observable, and regression-proof.

## Why this framing
- The defect is **delivery of recovery**, not detection: detection worked (heartbeat + stuck flag are in the ledger). Retracted framing: "add a stuck watchdog" — it exists (gh-1054); what's missing is the guarantee that the follow-up fires in every build/mode and that the model actually receives the nudge.
- The user-visible symptom ("session hung until I wrote как дела") is the deadlock: recovery nudges queue between turns, but the turn never ends because the model is blocked inside the very call that needs recovery. Only inbound user steering breaks the loop (foreground soft-yield).

## Architecture
- Components: **stuck supervisor** (`stuck_tool.dart` config + `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart` state machine: heartbeats at half-threshold → `tool_stuck` at threshold → `StuckFollowUpMode.autonomous` cancel → bounded retry → background-convert via the bash soft-yield path), **execution env** (`LocalShell` exec — no default timeout for no-timeout calls), **steering/inbox delivery** (notices flush at turn boundaries), **session ledger** (`tool_heartbeat` / `tool_stuck` custom records).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (escalation is unconditional):** on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.
  - **I2 (recovery budget):** wall-clock from `tool_stuck` to "turn continues" ≤ `cancelGrace + retry budget + conversion overhead` (bounded, config-named); exceeding it produces an **escalation record** naming the call — never silence.
  - **I3 (nudge reaches the model):** the watchdog notice is delivered to the model AT conversion time (rides the background-job result/nudge), not queued behind the blocked turn it is supposed to unblock.
  - **I4 (stuck ⇒ evidence):** in every session ledger, a `tool_stuck` record is followed within the recovery budget by exactly one of: background-job record (converted), retry record, or escalation record. **No orphan `tool_stuck` is a valid end state.**
  - **I5 (forensics):** session header records the fa **version** — today the dmtools session carries only a schema `version:3`, so "which build behaved how" is unanswerable post-mortem.

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autonomous cancel/retry/convert on `tool_stuck` in ALL modes | **core** | the gap itself; `advisory` = explicit config opt-out only (I1) |
| Watchdog nudge delivered at conversion time | **core** | I3; rides the soft-yield result the model actually sees |
| Recovery-budget bound + escalation record on overrun | **core** | I2; names call, duration, partial output |
| Ledger invariant: no orphan `tool_stuck` | **core** | I4; offline REG over real session JSONLs |
| fa version in session header | **core** | I5; forensics for "was the fix deployed?" |
| Per-tool stuck policy overrides (declared timeouts feed the threshold — exists) | second tier | verify long `flutter test` style declarations still suppress pestering (no false positives) |
| Cancellation of non-bash tools (LSP, MCP) on stuck | second tier | same state machine, tool-agnostic; bash is the proven path |
| External watchdog (factory trace-staleness) interplay | excluded | gh-1054 already sits inside the 10-min factory net; no changes |

## Security (self-recovery is a privilege escalation surface — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: a hung call can be *manufactured* (a malicious/broken command that blocks forever) to bait the supervisor into blind retries. Impossible-by-construction: the supervisor retries **once**, converts to background **once**, and never re-executes on its own schedule beyond that budget (I2) — no infinite retry amplification.
- Instruction hierarchy: the recovery path runs the SAME command under the SAME approval gates; conversion to background never bypasses approvals or expands the command. The nudge text is harness-authored system data — the stuck call's partial output rides it as data, redacted through the normal pipeline.
- Exfiltration gate: none opened by this card — recovery adds no new egress; background-converted jobs keep the existing `bash_job` visibility (logs on disk, `bash_job output`).
- Defense in depth: factory-side trace-staleness watchdog stays as the outer net; model obedience to the nudge is hygiene — the state machine acts regardless.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — deterministic repro of the incident: a bash call that blocks forever (sleep-forever fixture / hung `git fetch` shaped) with no declared timeout → at the 300 s floor `tool_stuck` fires; within the recovery budget the call is cancelled, retried once, converted to background; **the same turn continues** with job id + log path, in interactive mode. Hook: IT with deterministic clock + fake shell.
- **AC2** — the model-facing nudge is delivered at conversion time: the turn's next model request contains the watchdog notice alongside the background-job result (I3). IT asserts the request payload.
- **AC3** — `advisory` mode still exists but ONLY via explicit config; default-config interactive sessions get autonomous recovery (I1). UT on config parsing + IT on mode gating.
- **AC4** — recovery-budget overrun produces an escalation record naming call/duration/partial output, never silence (I2). IT with a cancel-refusing fake executor.
- **AC5** — ledger REG: fixture session (the anonymized dmtools timeline below) asserts `tool_stuck` ⇒ follow-up record within budget (I4); CI job runs this REG over pinned fixtures + property-generates orphan-stuck scenarios — **red REG blocks merge**.
- **AC6** — session header carries the fa version (I5); UT on the writer, IT on resume.
- **AC7** — no false-positive regressions: a declared-15-min `flutter test`-shaped call (timeout declared, running 6 min) is NOT stuck (threshold = factor × declared); existing tests green unchanged.

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-*` — config: floor/factor/heartbeat/cancelGrace/advisory parsing; budget math (I2); version writer (AC6).
- `IT-*` — supervisor state machine on a deterministic clock: AC1 full arc; AC2 payload; AC3 gating; AC4 escalation; AC7 non-stuck long call.
- `E2E-1` — real host: interactive session, `bash` that hangs on a pipe-read, 1.0.58x build → run self-recovers, transcript shows heartbeat → stuck → background-convert → continued turn (recorded as a pinned golden in docs).
- `REG-1` — offline ledger scanner (`I4`): CI job scanning pinned real-session fixtures (incl. the dmtools incident shape) + g…

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against

  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout

  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) …

- Behavior change: default-config REPL/TUI sessions now auto-cancel a stuck call, retry once, and convert the retry to a background job instead of flag-and-wait; owners wanting flag-only set `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`.

blocks.text:
# gh-1632: [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it

## Description

## Goal — stuck-call recovery that actually fires (v1)
One sentence: **a `tool_stuck` flag must always escalate — cancel → retry once → convert-to-background — so a hung tool call never outlives its own stuck threshold by more than the recovery budget; the model gets told and keeps working without a human poking the session.**

Observed failure (dmtools factory session `01a13fdc…`, 2026-10-15, fa **1.0.580**): a foreground `bash` call (work in `dmtools-agents`, incl. `git fetch` — network freeze or ssh/credential prompt with no tty) started 17:05:52Z, produced zero output. The liveness layer worked as documented — `tool_heartbeat` records every minute from 17:08:52, `tool_stuck` at **17:10:52** (= the 300 s floor, no declared timeout). Then **nothing**: the call sat hung for **27 minutes**. The `[liveness watchdog]` system notice reached the model only at **17:32:44** — 10 s after the OWNER's manual steering («как дела?», 17:32:34) soft-yielded the call to a background job. The agent then self-recovered in ~40 s (stopped the dead job, finished the task). gh-1054's supervision (heartbeats, stuck flag, autonomous cancel/retry/convert state machine in `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart`) either did not run in this build/mode or failed to fire — the goal is to make the escalation unconditional, observable, and regression-proof.

## Why this framing
- The defect is **delivery of recovery**, not detection: detection worked (heartbeat + stuck flag are in the ledger). Retracted framing: "add a stuck watchdog" — it exists (gh-1054); what's missing is the guarantee that the follow-up fires in every build/mode and that the model actually receives the nudge.
- The user-visible symptom ("session hung until I wrote как дела") is the deadlock: recovery nudges queue between turns, but the turn never ends because the model is blocked inside the very call that needs recovery. Only inbound user steering breaks the loop (foreground soft-yield).

## Architecture
- Components: **stuck supervisor** (`stuck_tool.dart` config + `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart` state machine: heartbeats at half-threshold → `tool_stuck` at threshold → `StuckFollowUpMode.autonomous` cancel → bounded retry → background-convert via the bash soft-yield path), **execution env** (`LocalShell` exec — no default timeout for no-timeout calls), **steering/inbox delivery** (notices flush at turn boundaries), **session ledger** (`tool_heartbeat` / `tool_stuck` custom records).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (escalation is unconditional):** on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.
  - **I2 (recovery budget):** wall-clock from `tool_stuck` to "turn continues" ≤ `cancelGrace + retry budget + conversion overhead` (bounded, config-named); exceeding it produces an **escalation record** naming the call — never silence.
  - **I3 (nudge reaches the model):** the watchdog notice is delivered to the model AT conversion time (rides the background-job result/nudge), not queued behind the blocked turn it is supposed to unblock.
  - **I4 (stuck ⇒ evidence):** in every session ledger, a `tool_stuck` record is followed within the recovery budget by exactly one of: background-job record (converted), retry record, or escalation record. **No orphan `tool_stuck` is a valid end state.**
  - **I5 (forensics):** session header records the fa **version** — today the dmtools session carries only a schema `version:3`, so "which build behaved how" is unanswerable post-mortem.

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autonomous cancel/retry/convert on `tool_stuck` in ALL modes | **core** | the gap itself; `advisory` = explicit config opt-out only (I1) |
| Watchdog nudge delivered at conversion time | **core** | I3; rides the soft-yield result the model actually sees |
| Recovery-budget bound + escalation record on overrun | **core** | I2; names call, duration, partial output |
| Ledger invariant: no orphan `tool_stuck` | **core** | I4; offline REG over real session JSONLs |
| fa version in session header | **core** | I5; forensics for "was the fix deployed?" |
| Per-tool stuck policy overrides (declared timeouts feed the threshold — exists) | second tier | verify long `flutter test` style declarations still suppress pestering (no false positives) |
| Cancellation of non-bash tools (LSP, MCP) on stuck | second tier | same state machine, tool-agnostic; bash is the proven path |
| External watchdog (factory trace-staleness) interplay | excluded | gh-1054 already sits inside the 10-min factory net; no changes |

## Security (self-recovery is a privilege escalation surface — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: a hung call can be *manufactured* (a malicious/broken command that blocks forever) to bait the supervisor into blind retries. Impossible-by-construction: the supervisor retries **once**, converts to background **once**, and never re-executes on its own schedule beyond that budget (I2) — no infinite retry amplification.
- Instruction hierarchy: the recovery path runs the SAME command under the SAME approval gates; conversion to background never bypasses approvals or expands the command. The nudge text is harness-authored system data — the stuck call's partial output rides it as data, redacted through the normal pipeline.
- Exfiltration gate: none opened by this card — recovery adds no new egress; background-converted jobs keep the existing `bash_job` visibility (logs on disk, `bash_job output`).
- Defense in depth: factory-side trace-staleness watchdog stays as the outer net; model obedience to the nudge is hygiene — the state machine acts regardless.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — deterministic repro of the incident: a bash call that blocks forever (sleep-forever fixture / hung `git fetch` shaped) with no declared timeout → at the 300 s floor `tool_stuck` fires; within the recovery budget the call is cancelled, retried once, converted to background; **the same turn continues** with job id + log path, in interactive mode. Hook: IT with deterministic clock + fake shell.
- **AC2** — the model-facing nudge is delivered at conversion time: the turn's next model request contains the watchdog notice alongside the background-job result (I3). IT asserts the request payload.
- **AC3** — `advisory` mode still exists but ONLY via explicit config; default-config interactive sessions get autonomous recovery (I1). UT on config parsing + IT on mode gating.
- **AC4** — recovery-budget overrun produces an escalation record naming call/duration/partial output, never silence (I2). IT with a cancel-refusing fake executor.
- **AC5** — ledger REG: fixture session (the anonymized dmtools timeline below) asserts `tool_stuck` ⇒ follow-up record within budget (I4); CI job runs this REG over pinned fixtures + property-generates orphan-stuck scenarios — **red REG blocks merge**.
- **AC6** — session header carries the fa version (I5); UT on the writer, IT on resume.
- **AC7** — no false-positive regressions: a declared-15-min `flutter test`-shaped call (timeout declared, running 6 min) is NOT stuck (threshold = factor × declared); existing tests green unchanged.

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-*` — config: floor/factor/heartbeat/cancelGrace/advisory parsing; budget math (I2); version writer (AC6).
- `IT-*` — supervisor state machine on a deterministic clock: AC1 full arc; AC2 payload; AC3 gating; AC4 escalation; AC7 non-stuck long call.
- `E2E-1` — real host: interactive session, `bash` that hangs on a pipe-read, 1.0.58x build → run self-recovers, transcript shows heartbeat → stuck → background-convert → continued turn (recorded as a pinned golden in docs).
- `REG-1` — offline ledger scanner (`I4`): CI job scanning pinned real-session fixtures (incl. the dmtools incident shape) + g…

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:

jobs:

  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /

  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and

  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch
  # hiccup, rev-list error) …

- **Title**: gh-1632 [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it
- **Author**: ai-teammate

## PR Description

Refs #1632 (partial — the I1 default fix only; the goal card stays open). Not closing: core-tier AC5 (offline orphan-`tool_stuck` ledger REG + red-blocks-merge CI job, I4) and AC6 (fa version in session header, I5) are not implemented in this PR — they remain open on gh-1632 and must land before the card closes.
### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` on every non-headless host when no explicit `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine is intact — the fa 1.0.580 incident session simply ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits `tool_stuck` and never cancels/retries/converts: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then 27 minutes of heartbeats until the owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Violated invariant I1 (`advisory` = explicit opt-out only, never an implicit interactive default).

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous default in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit `agent.stuckTool:` still wins, so `followUp: advisory` stays a deliberate opt-out. Config persistence unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` + `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` gh-1632 I1 tests — failed pre-fix (`Expected: autonomous, Actual: advisory`), pass post-fix.
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (the CI per-PR gate): 10986 passed, 10 skipped (env-conditional), 0 failures.

### Notes

- Behavior change: default-config REPL/TUI sessions now auto-cancel a stuck call, retry once, and convert the retry to a background job instead of flag-and-wait; owners wanting flag-only set `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`.
- Thresholds untouched — a declared-15-min `flutter test` running 6 min is still not stuck (AC7). Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape; the 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner.
- Adjacent gap, unchanged: the desktop-app wiring passes the raw config, so an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all — it never emits `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.

# gh-1632: [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it

## Description

## Goal — stuck-call recovery that actually fires (v1)
One sentence: **a `tool_stuck` flag must always escalate — cancel → retry once → convert-to-background — so a hung tool call never outlives its own stuck threshold by more than the recovery budget; the model gets told and keeps working without a human poking the session.**

Observed failure (dmtools factory session `01a13fdc…`, 2026-10-15, fa **1.0.580**): a foreground `bash` call (work in `dmtools-agents`, incl. `git fetch` — network freeze or ssh/credential prompt with no tty) started 17:05:52Z, produced zero output. The liveness layer worked as documented — `tool_heartbeat` records every minute from 17:08:52, `tool_stuck` at **17:10:52** (= the 300 s floor, no declared timeout). Then **nothing**: the call sat hung for **27 minutes**. The `[liveness watchdog]` system notice reached the model only at **17:32:44** — 10 s after the OWNER's manual steering («как дела?», 17:32:34) soft-yielded the call to a background job. The agent then self-recovered in ~40 s (stopped the dead job, finished the task). gh-1054's supervision (heartbeats, stuck flag, autonomous cancel/retry/convert state machine in `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart`) either did not run in this build/mode or failed to fire — the goal is to make the escalation unconditional, observable, and regression-proof.

## Why this framing
- The defect is **delivery of recovery**, not detection: detection worked (heartbeat + stuck flag are in the ledger). Retracted framing: "add a stuck watchdog" — it exists (gh-1054); what's missing is the guarantee that the follow-up fires in every build/mode and that the model actually receives the nudge.
- The user-visible symptom ("session hung until I wrote как дела") is the deadlock: recovery nudges queue between turns, but the turn never ends because the model is blocked inside the very call that needs recovery. Only inbound user steering breaks the loop (foreground soft-yield).

## Architecture
- Components: **stuck supervisor** (`stuck_tool.dart` config + `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart` state machine: heartbeats at half-threshold → `tool_stuck` at threshold → `StuckFollowUpMode.autonomous` cancel → bounded retry → background-convert via the bash soft-yield path), **execution env** (`LocalShell` exec — no default timeout for no-timeout calls), **steering/inbox delivery** (notices flush at turn boundaries), **session ledger** (`tool_heartbeat` / `tool_stuck` custom records).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (escalation is unconditional):** on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.
  - **I2 (recovery budget):** wall-clock from `tool_stuck` to "turn continues" ≤ `cancelGrace + retry budget + conversion overhead` (bounded, config-named); exceeding it produces an **escalation record** naming the call — never silence.
  - **I3 (nudge reaches the model):** the watchdog notice is delivered to the model AT conversion time (rides the background-job result/nudge), not queued behind the blocked turn it is supposed to unblock.
  - **I4 (stuck ⇒ evidence):** in every session ledger, a `tool_stuck` record is followed within the recovery budget by exactly one of: background-job record (converted), retry record, or escalation record. **No orphan `tool_stuck` is a valid end state.**
  - **I5 (forensics):** session header records the fa **version** — today the dmtools session carries only a schema `version:3`, so "which build behaved how" is unanswerable post-mortem.

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autonomous cancel/retry/convert on `tool_stuck` in ALL modes | **core** | the gap itself; `advisory` = explicit config opt-out only (I1) |
| Watchdog nudge delivered at conversion time | **core** | I3; rides the soft-yield result the model actually sees |
| Recovery-budget bound + escalation record on overrun | **core** | I2; names call, duration, partial output |
| Ledger invariant: no orphan `tool_stuck` | **core** | I4; offline REG over real session JSONLs |
| fa version in session header | **core** | I5; forensics for "was the fix deployed?" |
| Per-tool stuck policy overrides (declared timeouts feed the threshold — exists) | second tier | verify long `flutter test` style declarations still suppress pestering (no false positives) |
| Cancellation of non-bash tools (LSP, MCP) on stuck | second tier | same state machine, tool-agnostic; bash is the proven path |
| External watchdog (factory trace-staleness) interplay | excluded | gh-1054 already sits inside the 10-min factory net; no changes |

## Security (self-recovery is a privilege escalation surface — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: a hung call can be *manufactured* (a malicious/broken command that blocks forever) to bait the supervisor into blind retries. Impossible-by-construction: the supervisor retries **once**, converts to background **once**, and never re-executes on its own schedule beyond that budget (I2) — no infinite retry amplification.
- Instruction hierarchy: the recovery path runs the SAME command under the SAME approval gates; conversion to background never bypasses approvals or expands the command. The nudge text is harness-authored system data — the stuck call's partial output rides it as data, redacted through the normal pipeline.
- Exfiltration gate: none opened by this card — recovery adds no new egress; background-converted jobs keep the existing `bash_job` visibility (logs on disk, `bash_job output`).
- Defense in depth: factory-side trace-staleness watchdog stays as the outer net; model obedience to the nudge is hygiene — the state machine acts regardless.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — deterministic repro of the incident: a bash call that blocks forever (sleep-forever fixture / hung `git fetch` shaped) with no declared timeout → at the 300 s floor `tool_stuck` fires; within the recovery budget the call is cancelled, retried once, converted to background; **the same turn continues** with job id + log path, in interactive mode. Hook: IT with deterministic clock + fake shell.
- **AC2** — the model-facing nudge is delivered at conversion time: the turn's next model request contains the watchdog notice alongside the background-job result (I3). IT asserts the request payload.
- **AC3** — `advisory` mode still exists but ONLY via explicit config; default-config interactive sessions get autonomous recovery (I1). UT on config parsing + IT on mode gating.
- **AC4** — recovery-budget overrun produces an escalation record naming call/duration/partial output, never silence (I2). IT with a cancel-refusing fake executor.
- **AC5** — ledger REG: fixture session (the anonymized dmtools timeline below) asserts `tool_stuck` ⇒ follow-up record within budget (I4); CI job runs this REG over pinned fixtures + property-generates orphan-stuck scenarios — **red REG blocks merge**.
- **AC6** — session header carries the fa version (I5); UT on the writer, IT on resume.
- **AC7** — no false-positive regressions: a declared-15-min `flutter test`-shaped call (timeout declared, running 6 min) is NOT stuck (threshold = factor × declared); existing tests green unchanged.

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-*` — config: floor/factor/heartbeat/cancelGrace/advisory parsing; budget math (I2); version writer (AC6).
- `IT-*` — supervisor state machine on a deterministic clock: AC1 full arc; AC2 payload; AC3 gating; AC4 escalation; AC7 non-stuck long call.
- `E2E-1` — real host: interactive session, `bash` that hangs on a pipe-read, 1.0.58x build → run self-recovers, transcript shows heartbeat → stuck → background-convert → continued turn (recorded as a pinned golden in docs).

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded

#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,

- **Title**: gh-1632 [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1632` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +59
- **Deletions**: -37
- **Created**: 2026-10-15T15:25:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-16T00:53:53Z

## PR Description

Refs #1632 (partial — the I1 default fix only; the goal card stays open). Not closing: core-tier AC5 (offline orphan-`tool_stuck` ledger REG + red-blocks-merge CI job, I4) and AC6 (fa version in session header, I5) are not implemented in this PR — they remain open on gh-1632 and must land before the card closes.
### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` on every non-headless host when no explicit `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine is intact — the fa 1.0.580 incident session simply ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits `tool_stuck` and never cancels/retries/converts: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then 27 minutes of heartbeats until the owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Violated invariant I1 (`advisory` = explicit opt-out only, never an implicit interactive default).

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous default in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit `agent.stuckTool:` still wins, so `followUp: advisory` stays a deliberate opt-out. Config persistence unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` + `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` gh-1632 I1 tests — failed pre-fix (`Expected: autonomous, Actual: advisory`), pass post-fix.
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (the CI per-PR gate): 10986 passed, 10 skipped (env-conditional), 0 failures.

### Notes

- Behavior change: default-config REPL/TUI sessions now auto-cancel a stuck call, retry once, and convert the retry to a background job instead of flag-and-wait; owners wanting flag-only set `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`.
- Thresholds untouched — a declared-15-min `flutter test` running 6 min is still not stuck (AC7). Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape; the 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner.
- Adjacent gap, unchanged: the desktop-app wiring passes the raw config, so an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all — it never emits `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.

blocks.text:
# gh-1632: [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it

## Description

## Goal — stuck-call recovery that actually fires (v1)
One sentence: **a `tool_stuck` flag must always escalate — cancel → retry once → convert-to-background — so a hung tool call never outlives its own stuck threshold by more than the recovery budget; the model gets told and keeps working without a human poking the session.**

Observed failure (dmtools factory session `01a13fdc…`, 2026-10-15, fa **1.0.580**): a foreground `bash` call (work in `dmtools-agents`, incl. `git fetch` — network freeze or ssh/credential prompt with no tty) started 17:05:52Z, produced zero output. The liveness layer worked as documented — `tool_heartbeat` records every minute from 17:08:52, `tool_stuck` at **17:10:52** (= the 300 s floor, no declared timeout). Then **nothing**: the call sat hung for **27 minutes**. The `[liveness watchdog]` system notice reached the model only at **17:32:44** — 10 s after the OWNER's manual steering («как дела?», 17:32:34) soft-yielded the call to a background job. The agent then self-recovered in ~40 s (stopped the dead job, finished the task). gh-1054's supervision (heartbeats, stuck flag, autonomous cancel/retry/convert state machine in `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart`) either did not run in this build/mode or failed to fire — the goal is to make the escalation unconditional, observable, and regression-proof.

## Why this framing
- The defect is **delivery of recovery**, not detection: detection worked (heartbeat + stuck flag are in the ledger). Retracted framing: "add a stuck watchdog" — it exists (gh-1054); what's missing is the guarantee that the follow-up fires in every build/mode and that the model actually receives the nudge.
- The user-visible symptom ("session hung until I wrote как дела") is the deadlock: recovery nudges queue between turns, but the turn never ends because the model is blocked inside the very call that needs recovery. Only inbound user steering breaks the loop (foreground soft-yield).

## Architecture
- Components: **stuck supervisor** (`stuck_tool.dart` config + `agent_loop_stuck_supervision.dart` state machine: heartbeats at half-threshold → `tool_stuck` at threshold → `StuckFollowUpMode.autonomous` cancel → bounded retry → background-convert via the bash soft-yield path), **execution env** (`LocalShell` exec — no default timeout for no-timeout calls), **steering/inbox delivery** (notices flush at turn boundaries), **session ledger** (`tool_heartbeat` / `tool_stuck` custom records).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (escalation is unconditional):** on any build where `tool_stuck` is emitted, the follow-up fires by default in EVERY mode (interactive included); `advisory` exists only as an explicit opt-out (`agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`), never as an implicit default for interactive sessions.
  - **I2 (recovery budget):** wall-clock from `tool_stuck` to "turn continues" ≤ `cancelGrace + retry budget + conversion overhead` (bounded, config-named); exceeding it produces an **escalation record** naming the call — never silence.
  - **I3 (nudge reaches the model):** the watchdog notice is delivered to the model AT conversion time (rides the background-job result/nudge), not queued behind the blocked turn it is supposed to unblock.
  - **I4 (stuck ⇒ evidence):** in every session ledger, a `tool_stuck` record is followed within the recovery budget by exactly one of: background-job record (converted), retry record, or escalation record. **No orphan `tool_stuck` is a valid end state.**
  - **I5 (forensics):** session header records the fa **version** — today the dmtools session carries only a schema `version:3`, so "which build behaved how" is unanswerable post-mortem.

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1551: slim the 2h schedule tick. The schedule is the release arming
  # mechanism (gh-1537 retired the post-merge main run), but a tick with
  # ZERO commits on main since the last v* tag has nothing to release —
  # running the full ~35-40 min quality gate for it is pure waste against
  # the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle (observed: run
  # 38147581679, 2026-10-11). This cheap pre-check (~10-30 s: one checkout
  # + git rev-list) compares main HEAD against the latest semver v* tag and
  # exports `pending`; every gate leg ANDs the output into its `if`, so an
  # empty tick short-circuits the whole graph in seconds — legs show
  # SKIPPED explicitly (visible in the run, never silently absent) and the
  # run stays green.
  #
  # Arms that must NEVER be blocked (gh-1551 AC3): v* tag pushes,
  # `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (releaseDryRun /
  # releaseDispatch — incl. every SM validation dispatch, which is a
  # workflow_dispatch on the PR head). All of them short-circuit to
  # pending=true BEFORE the checkout — they do not even pay the fetch, and
  # the gate graph is byte-identical to gh-1537 for them.
  #
  # Fail-open (AC4): `pending` defaults to true and is flipped to false
  # only inside the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check (tag fetch

project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1635
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1635
- **Title**: gh-1632 [GOAL] Stuck-call recovery that fires: tool_stuck must escalate to cancel/retry/background-convert — fa 1.0.580 hung 27 min on a dead git fetch until a human poked it
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1632` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +59
- **Deletions**: -37
- **Created**: 2026-10-15T15:25:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-16T00:53:53Z

## PR Description

Refs #1632 (partial — the I1 default fix only; the goal card stays open). Not closing: core-tier AC5 (offline orphan-`tool_stuck` ledger REG + red-blocks-merge CI job, I4) and AC6 (fa version in session header, I5) are not implemented in this PR — they remain open on gh-1632 and must land before the card closes.
### Root Cause

- `AgentCliConfig.effectiveStuckTool()` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`) forced `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` on every non-headless host when no explicit `agent.stuckTool:` was configured. The gh-1054 supervision machine is intact — the fa 1.0.580 incident session simply ran it in advisory mode, where the threshold only emits `tool_stuck` and never cancels/retries/converts: stuck flag at 17:10:52, then 27 minutes of heartbeats until the owner's manual steering soft-yielded the call. Violated invariant I1 (`advisory` = explicit opt-out only, never an implicit interactive default).

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_config.dart`: `effectiveStuckTool()` now returns the autonomous default in EVERY mode when unconfigured; explicit `agent.stuckTool:` still wins, so `followUp: advisory` stays a deliberate opt-out. Config persistence unchanged (defaults are never written).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` + `test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` gh-1632 I1 tests — failed pre-fix (`Expected: autonomous, Actual: advisory`), pass post-fix.
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (the CI per-PR gate): 10986 passed, 10 skipped (env-conditional), 0 failures.

### Notes

- Behavior change: default-config REPL/TUI sessions now auto-cancel a stuck call, retry once, and convert the retry to a background job instead of flag-and-wait; owners wanting flag-only set `agent.stuckTool.followUp: advisory`.
- Thresholds untouched — a declared-15-min `flutter test` running 6 min is still not stuck (AC7). Recovery budget stays the shipped gh-1054 shape; the 1.5×-threshold cap sketch is left to the owner.
- Adjacent gap, unchanged: the desktop-app wiring passes the raw config, so an unconfigured app host gets no supervision at all — it never emits `tool_stuck`, so I1 is not violated; defaulting it is a separate decision.
