{"content":"# Rework — validation CI red on head `dc3cdffb` fixed

## Issues/Notes

- **CI red (blocking, this round's trigger):** validation run [38830911279](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38830911279) on head `dc3cdffb` failed `Core tests (shard 3/4)` (the `Quality gate` aggregate failed only because of that leg). The one failing test:
  `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time`, best doubling ratio **3.31x** vs the 3.2 bound (`2943 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped` in the shard).
- **Root cause — sustained runner contention, not a wrap regression.** The same assertion red on a second distinct head within one hour (run 38824807299, shard 0, ratio 3.35x), while the sibling absolute bounds (`1M cells < 100ms`, hard-cut) passed in the same shards. The growth harness already gated on the min ratio across 3 attempts (gh-1532), but each attempt still sampled each size with a **median of 5 timed runs**: a contention window spanning ≥3 of the doubled size's 5 runs in *every* attempt inflates every attempt median and the cross-attempt min cannot rescue it. That is exactly the observed shape — a sustained steal window on the shared `ubuntu-24.04-arm` pool, with the doubled (longer, 2× exposure) samples absorbing the preemptions and the small samples stable.
- This is a continuation of the known flake series on this assertion (#1530/#1531 → gh-1532 fix #1534; FLAKE-SYSTEMIC #1543). As with every prior round, the fix hardens the measurement; the 3.2 detection threshold (linear ≈ 2x, quadratic ≈ 4x+) is unchanged and no quarantine is applied — the guard stays live in the gate.
- Prior review findings re-verified at this head: the three stale dartdocs carry the gh-1632 I1 default; the PR body uses `Refs #1632` (no auto-close; AC5/AC6 stay open on the goal card); `git diff origin/main...HEAD` contains **zero** `apiKey` fixture-line changes in both test files.

## Approach

TDD, test-only change — production code untouched (`wrapAnsiLine` is proven correct by the passing absolute bounds):

1. **RED** — added a deterministic reproduction of the live failure shape using the file's `ContendedClock` (the gh-1532 precedent): 4 of the 5 doubled-size timed runs spiked with 30 ms of fake preemption in *each* of the 3 attempts (spike indices `{6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}` of the 30-call layout, layout-guarded like the existing preemption test). On the pre-fix harness this fails with ratio ~7x — median-of-5 takes a spiked value in every attempt — mirroring the live reds.
2. **GREEN** — `expectLinearGrowth` now samples each size with the new `minWrapMs` (fastest of the 5 timed runs) instead of the median. Contention can only ADD wall time, so the fastest observed run is the least-contaminated per-size estimate — the same principle gh-1532 applied across attempts, applied within them. A median needs a majority of clean runs; a min needs exactly one. A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).
3. Wall time is unchanged (same warm-up + 5 timed runs per size per attempt), so the shard duration budget is untouched.

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `minWrapMs` helper; `expectLinearGrowth` switched median→min per size; new deterministic sustained-contention regression test; header/contract comments updated to the new statistic (no stale "median" claims left).

A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).

{"content":"# Rework — validation CI red on head `dc3cdffb` fixed

## Issues/Notes

- **CI red (blocking, this round's trigger):** validation run [38830911279](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38830911279) on head `dc3cdffb` failed `Core tests (shard 3/4)` (the `Quality gate` aggregate failed only because of that leg). The one failing test:

The growth harness already gated on the min ratio across 3 attempts (gh-1532), but each attempt still sampled each size with a **median of 5 timed runs**: a contention window spanning ≥3 of the doubled size's 5 runs in *every* attempt inflates every attempt median and the cross-attempt min cannot rescue it. - This is a continuation of the known flake series on this assertion (#1530/#1531 → gh-1532 fix #1534; FLAKE-SYSTEMIC #1543). As with every prior round, the fix hardens the measurement; the 3.2 detection threshold (linear ≈ 2x, quadratic ≈ 4x+) is unchanged and no quarantine is applied — the guard stays live in the gate.

A median needs a majority of clean runs; a min needs exactly one. A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).
3. Wall time is unchanged (same warm-up + 5 timed runs per size per attempt), so the shard duration budget is untouched.

{"content":"# Rework — validation CI red on head `dc3cdffb` fixed

## Issues/Notes

- **CI red (blocking, this round's trigger):** validation run [38830911279](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38830911279) on head `dc3cdffb` failed `Core tests (shard 3/4)` (the `Quality gate` aggregate failed only because of that leg). The one failing test:

- **Root cause — sustained runner contention, not a wrap regression.** The same assertion red on a second distinct head within one hour (run 38824807299, shard 0, ratio 3.35x), while the sibling absolute bounds (`1M cells < 100ms`, hard-cut) passed in the same shards. The growth harness already gated on the min ratio across 3 attempts (gh-1532), but each attempt still sampled each size with a **median of 5 timed runs**: a contention window spanning ≥3 of the doubled size's 5 runs in *every* attempt inflates every attempt median and the cross-attempt min cannot rescue it. That is exactly the observed shape — a sustained steal window on the shared `ubuntu-24.04-arm` pool, with the doubled (longer, 2× exposure) samples absorbing the preemptions and the small samples stable.
- This is a continuation of the known flake series on this assertion (#1530/#1531 → gh-1532 fix #1534; FLAKE-SYSTEMIC #1543). As with every prior round, the fix hardens the measurement; the 3.2 detection threshold (linear ≈ 2x, quadratic ≈ 4x+) is unchanged and no quarantine is applied — the guard stays live in the gate.
- Prior review findings re-verified at this head: the three stale dartdocs carry the gh-1632 I1 default; the PR body uses `Refs #1632` (no auto-close; AC5/AC6 stay open on the goal card); `git diff origin/main...HEAD` contains **zero** `apiKey` fixture-line changes in both test files.

## Approach

TDD, test-only change — production code untouched (`wrapAnsiLine` is proven correct by the passing absolute bounds):

1. **RED** — added a deterministic reproduction of the live failure shape using the file's `ContendedClock` (the gh-1532 precedent): 4 of the 5 doubled-size timed runs spiked with 30 ms of fake preemption in *each* of the 3 attempts (spike indices `{6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}` of the 30-call layout, layout-guarded like the existing preemption test). On the pre-fix harness this fails with ratio ~7x — median-of-5 takes a spiked value in every attempt — mirroring the live reds.
2. **GREEN** — `expectLinearGrowth` now samples each size with the new `minWrapMs` (fastest of the 5 timed runs) instead of the median. Contention can only ADD wall time, so the fastest observed run is the least-contaminated per-size estimate — the same principle gh-1532 applied across attempts, applied within them. A median needs a majority of clean runs; a min needs exactly one. A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).
3. Wall time is unchanged (same warm-up + 5 timed runs per size per attempt), so the shard duration budget is untouched.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `minWrapMs` helper; `expectLinearGrowth` switched median→min per size; new deterministic sustained-contention regression test; header/contract comments updated to the new statistic (no stale "median" claims left).

## Test Coverage

- New test `growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)`: **fails on the pre-fix harness (ratio 7.0x), passes post-fix** — the exact sustained-contention shape behind both live reds (runs 38824807299, 38830911279).
- Existing discriminators still green: gh-1532 preemption spike test, gh-1460 pause-proof arithmetic test, degenerate-flat rejection test (the guard stays meaningful under the min statistic).

- Full per-PR gate: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` → RESULT_PLACEHOLDER.

1. **RED** — added a deterministic reproduction of the live failure shape using the file's `ContendedClock` (the gh-1532 precedent): 4 of the 5 doubled-size timed runs spiked with 30 ms of fake preemption in *each* of the 3 attempts (spike indices `{6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}` of the 30-call layout, layout-guarded like the existing preemption test). On the pre-fix harness this fails with ratio ~7x — median-of-5 takes a spiked value in every attempt — mirroring the live reds.
2. **GREEN** — `expectLinearGrowth` now samples each size with the new `minWrapMs` (fastest of the 5 timed runs) instead of the median. Contention can only ADD wall time, so the fastest observed run is the least-contaminated per-size estimate — the same principle gh-1532 applied across attempts, applied within them. A median needs a majority of clean runs; a min needs exactly one. A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).
3. Wall time is unchanged (same warm-up + 5 timed runs per size per attempt), so the shard duration budget is untouched.

{"content":"# Rework — validation CI red on head `dc3cdffb` fixed

- **CI red (blocking, this round's trigger):** validation run [38830911279](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38830911279) on head `dc3cdffb` failed `Core tests (shard 3/4)` (the `Quality gate` aggregate failed only because of that leg). The one failing test:

- **Root cause — sustained runner contention, not a wrap regression.** The same assertion red on a second distinct head within one hour (run 38824807299, shard 0, ratio 3.35x), while the sibling absolute bounds (`1M cells < 100ms`, hard-cut) passed in the same shards. The growth harness already gated on the min ratio across 3 attempts (gh-1532), but each attempt still sampled each size with a **median of 5 timed runs**: a contention window spanning ≥3 of the doubled size's 5 runs in *every* attempt inflates every attempt median and the cross-attempt min cannot rescue it. That is exactly the observed shape — a sustained steal window on the shared `ubuntu-24.04-arm` pool, with the doubled (longer, 2× exposure) samples absorbing the preemptions and the small samples stable.
- This is a continuation of the known flake series on this assertion (#1530/#1531 → gh-1532 fix #1534; FLAKE-SYSTEMIC #1543). As with every prior round, the fix hardens the measurement; the 3.2 detection threshold (linear ≈ 2x, quadratic ≈ 4x+) is unchanged and no quarantine is applied — the guard stays live in the gate.
- Prior review findings re-verified at this head: the three stale dartdocs carry the gh-1632 I1 default; the PR body uses `Refs #1632` (no auto-close; AC5/AC6 stay open on the goal card); `git diff origin/main...HEAD` contains **zero** `apiKey` fixture-line changes in both test files.

1. **RED** — added a deterministic reproduction of the live failure shape using the file's `ContendedClock` (the gh-1532 precedent): 4 of the 5 doubled-size timed runs spiked with 30 ms of fake preemption in *each* of the 3 attempts (spike indices `{6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}` of the 30-call layout, layout-guarded like the existing preemption test). Contention can only ADD wall time, so the fastest observed run is the least-contaminated per-size estimate — the same principle gh-1532 applied across attempts, applied within them. A median needs a majority of clean runs; a min needs exactly one. A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).
3. Wall time is unchanged (same warm-up + 5 timed runs per size per attempt), so the shard duration budget is untouched.

The suite is still in early stages (no output yet — it buffers). While waiting, let me commit the change locally (not push yet — wait for the suite). Actually, let me hold the commit until the suite is green, per discipline (if the suite finds an issue I'd amend).

Let me also double-check one potential concern with my change: in `expectLinearGrowth`, `maxRatio` now tracks max of min-based ratios. Is there a scenario where live jitter makes maxRatio ≤ 1.5 spuriously (failing the degenerate guard)? maxRatio ≤ 1.5 requires every attempt's min-doubled / min-small ≤ 1.5 — i.e., doubling input costs <1.5x time in EVERY attempt. On honest hardware a linear wrap measures ~1.8-2.2x. Could a bizarre CPU (turbo warm-up on the small run) compress it below 1.5 in all 3 attempts? The small run is measured first, doubled second — the doubled run may benefit from warmer caches/JIT while the small run pays cold costs... but each size has its own untimed warm-up, so steady state both. Thermal throttling would slow the LATER (doubled) runs → higher ratio, not lower. Frequency boost decay over the test: small measured early at boost clocks, doubled later at reduced clocks → ratio could compress. Magnitude: modern runners hold clocks within ~10-20% over a 2s window; ratio 2.0 × 0.8 = 1.6 > 1.5, still clear. And this guard (max > 1.5) existed before with medians — the same exposure. Not a new risk class; the file's own history shows the max guard never false-fired (the failures were always on the min/upper side). OK.

Second concern — could min-of-5 per size mask a REAL superlinear regression that only inflates SOME doubled runs? A per-row rescan regression inflates EVERY doubled run deterministically (it's algorithmic, not environmental). Min inflates too → trips. Only environmental inflation hits subsets — which is exactly what we WANT to ignore. Correct semantics.

Third — `minWrapMs` wall-clock: same 5 runs as before; no wall-time change to the suite. Good — shard duration budget unaffected.

Fourth: check nothing else uses `expectLinearGrowth` or `medianWrapMs` outside this file (they're file-local helpers; but bench/ or other tests might import?). Let me grep.

Is there a scenario where live jitter makes maxRatio ≤ 1.5 spuriously (failing the degenerate guard)? maxRatio ≤ 1.5 requires every attempt's min-doubled / min-small ≤ 1.5 — i.e., doubling input costs <1.5x time in EVERY attempt. On honest hardware a linear wrap measures ~1.8-2.2x. Could a bizarre CPU (turbo warm-up on the small run) compress it below 1.5 in all 3 attempts? The small run is measured first, doubled second — the doubled run may benefit from warmer caches/JIT while the small run pays cold costs... but each size has its own untimed warm-up, so steady state both. Thermal throttling would slow the LATER (doubled) runs → higher ratio, not lower. Frequency boost decay over the test: small measured early at boost clocks, doubled later at reduced clocks → ratio could compress. Magnitude: modern runners hold clocks within ~10-20% over a 2s window; ratio 2.0 × 0.8 = 1.6 > 1.5, still clear. And this guard (max > 1.5) existed before with medians — the same exposure. Not a new risk class; the file's own history shows the max guard never false-fired (the failures were always on the min/upper side). OK.

Second concern — could min-of-5 per size mask a REAL superlinear regression that only inflates SOME doubled runs? A per-row rescan regression inflates EVERY doubled run deterministically (it's algorithmic, not environmental). Min inflates too → trips. Only environmental inflation hits subsets — which is exactly what we WANT to ignore. Correct semantics.

{"content":"# Rework — validation CI red on head `dc3cdffb` fixed

## Issues/Notes

- **CI red (blocking, this round's trigger):** validation run [38830911279](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38830911279) on head `dc3cdffb` failed `Core tests (shard 3/4)` (the `Quality gate` aggregate failed only because of that leg). The one failing test:
  `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time`, best doubling ratio **3.31x** vs the 3.2 bound (`2943 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped` in the shard).
- **Root cause — sustained runner contention, not a wrap regression.** The same assertion red on a second distinct head within one hour (run 38824807299, shard 0, ratio 3.35x), while the sibling absolute bounds (`1M cells < 100ms`, hard-cut) passed in the same shards. The growth harness already gated on the min ratio across 3 attempts (gh-1532), but each attempt still sampled each size with a **median of 5 timed runs**: a contention window spanning ≥3 of the doubled size's 5 runs in *every* attempt inflates every attempt median and the cross-attempt min cannot rescue it. That is exactly the observed shape — a sustained steal window on the shared `ubuntu-24.04-arm` pool, with the doubled (longer, 2× exposure) samples absorbing the preemptions and the small samples stable.
- This is a continuation of the known flake series on this assertion (#1530/#1531 → gh-1532 fix #1534; FLAKE-SYSTEMIC #1543). As with every prior round, the fix hardens the measurement; the 3.2 detection threshold (linear ≈ 2x, quadratic ≈ 4x+) is unchanged and no quarantine is applied — the guard stays live in the gate.
- Prior review findings re-verified at this head: the three stale dartdocs carry the gh-1632 I1 default; the PR body uses `Refs #1632` (no auto-close; AC5/AC6 stay open on the goal card); `git diff origin/main...HEAD` contains **zero** `apiKey` fixture-line changes in both test files.

## Approach

TDD, test-only change — production code untouched (`wrapAnsiLine` is proven correct by the passing absolute bounds):

1. **RED** — added a deterministic reproduction of the live failure shape using the file's `ContendedClock` (the gh-1532 precedent): 4 of the 5 doubled-size timed runs spiked with 30 ms of fake preemption in *each* of the 3 attempts (spike indices `{6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}` of the 30-call layout, layout-guarded like the existing preemption test). On the pre-fix harness this fails with ratio ~7x — median-of-5 takes a spiked value in every attempt — mirroring the live reds.
2. **GREEN** — `expectLinearGrowth` now samples each size with the new `minWrapMs` (fastest of the 5 timed runs) instead of the median. Contention can only ADD wall time, so the fastest observed run is the least-contaminated per-size estimate — the same principle gh-1532 applied across attempts, applied within them. A median needs a majority of clean runs; a min needs exactly one. A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).
3. Wall time is unchanged (same warm-up + 5 timed runs per size per attempt), so the shard duration budget is untouched.

{"content":"# Rework — validation CI red on head `dc3cdffb` fixed

## Issues/Notes

- **CI red (blocking, this round's trigger):** validation run [38830911279](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38830911279) on head `dc3cdffb` failed `Core tests (shard 3/4)` (the `Quality gate` aggregate failed only because of that leg). The one failing test:
  `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time`, best doubling ratio **3.31x** vs the 3.2 bound (`2943 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped` in the shard).
- **Root cause — sustained runner contention, not a wrap regression.** The same assertion red on a second distinct head within one hour (run 38824807299, shard 0, ratio 3.35x), while the sibling absolute bounds (`1M cells < 100ms`, hard-cut) passed in the same shards. The growth harness already gated on the min ratio across 3 attempts (gh-1532), but each attempt still sampled each size with a **median of 5 timed runs**: a contention window spanning ≥3 of the doubled size's 5 runs in *every* attempt inflates every attempt median and the cross-attempt min cannot rescue it. That is exactly the observed shape — a sustained steal window on the shared `ubuntu-24.04-arm` pool, with the doubled (longer, 2× exposure) samples absorbing the preemptions and the small samples stable.
- This is a continuation of the known flake series on this assertion (#1530/#1531 → gh-1532 fix #1534; FLAKE-SYSTEMIC #1543). As with every prior round, the fix hardens the measurement; the 3.2 detection threshold (linear ≈ 2x, quadratic ≈ 4x+) is unchanged and no quarantine is applied — the guard stays live in the gate.
- Prior review findings re-verified at this head: the three stale dartdocs carry the gh-1632 I1 default; the PR body uses `Refs #1632` (no auto-close; AC5/AC6 stay open on the goal card); `git diff origin/main...HEAD` contains **zero** `apiKey` fixture-line changes in both test files.

## Approach

TDD, test-only change — production code untouched (`wrapAnsiLine` is proven correct by the passing absolute bounds):

1. **RED** — added a deterministic reproduction of the live failure shape using the file's `ContendedClock` (the gh-1532 precedent): 4 of the 5 doubled-size timed runs spiked with 30 ms of fake preemption in *each* of the 3 attempts (spike indices `{6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}` of the 30-call layout, layout-guarded like the existing preemption test). On the pre-fix harness this fails with ratio ~7x — median-of-5 takes a spiked value in every attempt — mirroring the live reds.
2. **GREEN** — `expectLinearGrowth` now samples each size with the new `minWrapMs` (fastest of the 5 timed runs) instead of the median. Contention can only ADD wall time, so the fastest observed run is the least-contaminated per-size estimate — the same principle gh-1532 applied across attempts, applied within them. A median needs a majority of clean runs; a min needs exactly one. A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).
3. Wall time is unchanged (same warm-up + 5 timed runs per size per attempt), so the shard duration budget is untouched.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `minWrapMs` helper; `expectLinearGrowth` switched median→min per size; new deterministic sustained-contention regression test; header/contract comments updated to the new statistic (no stale "median" claims left).

## Test Coverage

- New test `growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)`: **fails on the pre-fix harness (ratio 7.0x), passes post-fix** — the exact sustained-contention shape behind both live reds (runs 38824807299, 38830911279).
- Existing discriminators still green: gh-1532 preemption spike test, gh-1460 pause-proof arithmetic test, degenerate-flat rejection test (the guard stays meaningful under the min statistic).

- PR suites re-run: `dart test test/cli/cli_config_test.dart test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` → 140 passed.
- Full per-PR gate: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` → RESULT_PLACEHOLDER.

{"content":"# Rework — validation CI red on head `dc3cdffb` fixed

## Issues/Notes

- **CI red (blocking, this round's trigger):** validation run [38830911279](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38830911279) on head `dc3cdffb` failed `Core tests (shard 3/4)` (the `Quality gate` aggregate failed only because of that leg). The one failing test:
  `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time`, best doubling ratio **3.31x** vs the 3.2 bound (`2943 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped` in the shard).
- **Root cause — sustained runner contention, not a wrap regression.** The same assertion red on a second distinct head within one hour (run 38824807299, shard 0, ratio 3.35x), while the sibling absolute bounds (`1M cells < 100ms`, hard-cut) passed in the same shards. The growth harness already gated on the min ratio across 3 attempts (gh-1532), but each attempt still sampled each size with a **median of 5 timed runs**: a contention window spanning ≥3 of the doubled size's 5 runs in *every* attempt inflates every attempt median and the cross-attempt min cannot rescue it. That is exactly the observed shape — a sustained steal window on the shared `ubuntu-24.04-arm` pool, with the doubled (longer, 2× exposure) samples absorbing the preemptions and the small samples stable.
- This is a continuation of the known flake series on this assertion (#1530/#1531 → gh-1532 fix #1534; FLAKE-SYSTEMIC #1543). As with every prior round, the fix hardens the measurement; the 3.2 detection threshold (linear ≈ 2x, quadratic ≈ 4x+) is unchanged and no quarantine is applied — the guard stays live in the gate.
- Prior review findings re-verified at this head: the three stale dartdocs carry the gh-1632 I1 default; the PR body uses `Refs #1632` (no auto-close; AC5/AC6 stay open on the goal card); `git diff origin/main...HEAD` contains **zero** `apiKey` fixture-line changes in both test files.

## Approach

TDD, test-only change — production code untouched (`wrapAnsiLine` is proven correct by the passing absolute bounds):

1. **RED** — added a deterministic reproduction of the live failure shape using the file's `ContendedClock` (the gh-1532 precedent): 4 of the 5 doubled-size timed runs spiked with 30 ms of fake preemption in *each* of the 3 attempts (spike indices `{6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}` of the 30-call layout, layout-guarded like the existing preemption test). On the pre-fix harness this fails with ratio ~7x — median-of-5 takes a spiked value in every attempt — mirroring the live reds.
2. **GREEN** — `expectLinearGrowth` now samples each size with the new `minWrapMs` (fastest of the 5 timed runs) instead of the median. Contention can only ADD wall time, so the fastest observed run is the least-contaminated per-size estimate — the same principle gh-1532 applied across attempts, applied within them. A median needs a majority of clean runs; a min needs exactly one. A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).
3. Wall time is unchanged (same warm-up + 5 timed runs per size per attempt), so the shard duration budget is untouched.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `minWrapMs` helper; `expectLinearGrowth` switched median→min per size; new deterministic sustained-contention regression test; header/contract comments updated to the new statistic (no stale "median" claims left).

## Test Coverage

- New test `growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)`: **fails on the pre-fix harness (ratio 7.0x), passes post-fix** — the exact sustained-contention shape behind both live reds (runs 38824807299, 38830911279).

- Full per-PR gate: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` → RESULT_PLACEHOLDER.

Let me also double-check one potential concern with my change: in `expectLinearGrowth`, `maxRatio` now tracks max of min-based ratios. Is there a scenario where live jitter makes maxRatio ≤ 1.5 spuriously (failing the degenerate guard)? maxRatio ≤ 1.5 requires every attempt's min-doubled / min-small ≤ 1.5 — i.e., doubling input costs <1.5x time in EVERY attempt. On honest hardware a linear wrap measures ~1.8-2.2x. Could a bizarre CPU (turbo warm-up on the small run) compress it below 1.5 in all 3 attempts? The small run is measured first, doubled second — the doubled run may benefit from warmer caches/JIT while the small run pays cold costs... but each size has its own untimed warm-up, so steady state both. Thermal throttling would slow the LATER (doubled) runs → higher ratio, not lower. Frequency boost decay over the test: small measured early at boost clocks, doubled later at reduced clocks → ratio could compress. Magnitude: modern runners hold clocks within ~10-20% over a 2s window; ratio 2.0 × 0.8 = 1.6 > 1.5, still clear. And this guard (max > 1.5) existed before with medians — the same exposure. ## Issues/Notes

- **CI red (blocking, this round's trigger):** validation run [38830911279](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38830911279) on head `dc3cdffb` failed `Core tests (shard 3/4)` (the `Quality gate` aggregate failed only because of that leg). The one failing test:

- **Root cause — sustained runner contention, not a wrap regression.** The same assertion red on a second distinct head within one hour (run 38824807299, shard 0, ratio 3.35x), while the sibling absolute bounds (`1M cells < 100ms`, hard-cut) passed in the same shards. The growth harness already gated on the min ratio across 3 attempts (gh-1532), but each attempt still sampled each size with a **median of 5 timed runs**: a contention window spanning ≥3 of the doubled size's 5 runs in *every* attempt inflates every attempt median and the cross-attempt min cannot rescue it. That is exactly the observed shape — a sustained steal window on the shared `ubuntu-24.04-arm` pool, with the doubled (longer, 2× exposure) samples absorbing the preemptions and the small samples stable.
- This is a continuation of the known flake series on this assertion (#1530/#1531 → gh-1532 fix #1534; FLAKE-SYSTEMIC #1543). As with every prior round, the fix hardens the measurement; the 3.2 detection threshold (linear ≈ 2x, quadratic ≈ 4x+) is unchanged and no quarantine is applied — the guard stays live in the gate.
- Prior review findings re-verified at this head: the three stale dartdocs carry the gh-1632 I1 default; the PR body uses `Refs #1632` (no auto-close; AC5/AC6 stay open on the goal card); `git diff origin/main...HEAD` contains **zero** `apiKey` fixture-line changes in both test files.

## Approach

TDD, test-only change — production code untouched (`wrapAnsiLine` is proven correct by the passing absolute bounds):

1. **RED** — added a deterministic reproduction of the live failure shape using the file's `ContendedClock` (the gh-1532 precedent): 4 of the 5 doubled-size timed runs spiked with 30 ms of fake preemption in *each* of the 3 attempts (spike indices `{6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}` of the 30-call layout, layout-guarded like the existing preemption test). On the pre-fix harness this fails with ratio ~7x — median-of-5 takes a spiked value in every attempt — mirroring the live reds.
2. **GREEN** — `expectLinearGrowth` now samples each size with the new `minWrapMs` (fastest of the 5 timed runs) instead of the median. Contention can only ADD wall time, so the fastest observed run is the least-contaminated per-size estimate — the same principle gh-1532 applied across attempts, applied within them. A median needs a majority of clean runs; a min needs exactly one. A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).
3. Wall time is unchanged (same warm-up + 5 timed runs per size per attempt), so the shard duration budget is untouched.

{"content":"# Rework — validation CI red on head `dc3cdffb` fixed

## Issues/Notes

- **CI red (blocking, this round's trigger):** validation run [38830911279](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38830911279) on head `dc3cdffb` failed `Core tests (shard 3/4)` (the `Quality gate` aggregate failed only because of that leg). The one failing test:
  `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time`, best doubling ratio **3.31x** vs the 3.2 bound (`2943 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped` in the shard).
- **Root cause — sustained runner contention, not a wrap regression.** The same assertion red on a second distinct head within one hour (run 38824807299, shard 0, ratio 3.35x), while the sibling absolute bounds (`1M cells < 100ms`, hard-cut) passed in the same shards. The growth harness already gated on the min ratio across 3 attempts (gh-1532), but each attempt still sampled each size with a **median of 5 timed runs**: a contention window spanning ≥3 of the doubled size's 5 runs in *every* attempt inflates every attempt median and the cross-attempt min cannot rescue it. That is exactly the observed shape — a sustained steal window on the shared `ubuntu-24.04-arm` pool, with the doubled (longer, 2× exposure) samples absorbing the preemptions and the small samples stable.
- This is a continuation of the known flake series on this assertion (#1530/#1531 → gh-1532 fix #1534; FLAKE-SYSTEMIC #1543). As with every prior round, the fix hardens the measurement; the 3.2 detection threshold (linear ≈ 2x, quadratic ≈ 4x+) is unchanged and no quarantine is applied — the guard stays live in the gate.
- Prior review findings re-verified at this head: the three stale dartdocs carry the gh-1632 I1 default; the PR body uses `Refs #1632` (no auto-close; AC5/AC6 stay open on the goal card); `git diff origin/main...HEAD` contains **zero** `apiKey` fixture-line changes in both test files.

## Approach

TDD, test-only change — production code untouched (`wrapAnsiLine` is proven correct by the passing absolute bounds):

1. **RED** — added a deterministic reproduction of the live failure shape using the file's `ContendedClock` (the gh-1532 precedent): 4 of the 5 doubled-size timed runs spiked with 30 ms of fake preemption in *each* of the 3 attempts (spike indices `{6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}` of the 30-call layout, layout-guarded like the existing preemption test). On the pre-fix harness this fails with ratio ~7x — median-of-5 takes a spiked value in every attempt — mirroring the live reds.
2. **GREEN** — `expectLinearGrowth` now samples each size with the new `minWrapMs` (fastest of the 5 timed runs) instead of the median. Contention can only ADD wall time, so the fastest observed run is the least-contaminated per-size estimate — the same principle gh-1532 applied across attempts, applied within them. A median needs a majority of clean runs; a min needs exactly one. A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).
3. Wall time is unchanged (same warm-up + 5 timed runs per size per attempt), so the shard duration budget is untouched.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `minWrapMs` helper; `expectLinearGrowth` switched median→min per size; new deterministic sustained-contention regression test; header/contract comments updated to the new statistic (no stale "median" claims left).

## Test Coverage

- New test `growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)`: **fails on the pre-fix harness (ratio 7.0x), passes post-fix** — the exact sustained-contention shape behind both live reds (runs 38824807299, 38830911279).
- Existing discriminators still green: gh-1532 preemption spike test, gh-1460 pause-proof arithmetic test, degenerate-flat rejection test (the guard stays meaningful under the min statistic).
- Full file: `dart test test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` → 10/10 passed; `dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings` clean; `dart format` clean.
- PR suites re-run: `dart test test/cli/cli_config_test.dart test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` → 140 passed.
- Full per-PR gate: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` → RESULT_PLACEHOLDER.

content.text:
# Rework — validation CI red on head `dc3cdffb` fixed (branch head now `5141afc65`)

## Issues/Notes

- **CI red (blocking, this round's trigger):** validation run [38830911279](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38830911279) on head `dc3cdffb` failed `Core tests (shard 3/4)` (the `Quality gate` aggregate failed only because of that leg). The one failing test:
  `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time`, best doubling ratio **3.31x** vs the 3.2 bound (`2943 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped` in the shard).
- **Root cause — sustained runner contention, not a wrap regression.** The same assertion red on a second distinct head within one hour (run 38824807299, shard 0, ratio 3.35x), while the sibling absolute bounds (`1M cells < 100ms`, hard-cut) passed in the same shards. The growth harness already gated on the min ratio across 3 attempts (gh-1532), but each attempt still sampled each size with a **median of 5 timed runs**: a contention window spanning ≥3 of the doubled size's 5 runs in *every* attempt inflates every attempt median and the cross-attempt min cannot rescue it. That is exactly the observed shape — a sustained steal window on the shared `ubuntu-24.04-arm` pool, with the doubled (longer, 2× exposure) samples absorbing the preemptions and the small samples stable.
- This is a continuation of the known flake series on this assertion (#1530/#1531 → gh-1532 fix #1534; FLAKE-SYSTEMIC #1543). As with every prior round, the fix hardens the measurement; the 3.2 detection threshold (linear ≈ 2x, quadratic ≈ 4x+) is unchanged and no quarantine is applied — the guard stays live in the gate.
- Prior review findings re-verified at this head: the three stale dartdocs carry the gh-1632 I1 default; the PR body uses `Refs #1632` (no auto-close; AC5/AC6 stay open on the goal card); `git diff origin/main...HEAD` contains **zero** `apiKey` fixture-line changes in both test files.

## Approach

TDD, test-only change — production code untouched (`wrapAnsiLine` is proven correct by the passing absolute bounds):

1. **RED** — added a deterministic reproduction of the live failure shape using the file's `ContendedClock` (the gh-1532 precedent): 4 of the 5 doubled-size timed runs spiked with 30 ms of fake preemption in *each* of the 3 attempts (spike indices `{6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}` of the 30-call layout, layout-guarded like the existing preemption test). On the pre-fix harness this fails with ratio ~7x — median-of-5 takes a spiked value in every attempt — mirroring the live reds.
2. **GREEN** — `expectLinearGrowth` now samples each size with the new `minWrapMs` (fastest of the 5 timed runs) instead of the median. Contention can only ADD wall time, so the fastest observed run is the least-contaminated per-size estimate — the same principle gh-1532 applied across attempts, applied within them. A median needs a majority of clean runs; a min needs exactly one. A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).
3. Wall time is unchanged (same warm-up + 5 timed runs per size per attempt), so the shard duration budget is untouched.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `minWrapMs` helper; `expectLinearGrowth` switched median→min per size; new deterministic sustained-contention regression test; header/contract comments updated to the new statistic (no stale "median" claims left).

## Test Coverage

- New test `growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)`: **fails on the pre-fix harness (ratio 7.0x), passes post-fix** — the exact sustained-contention shape behind both live reds (runs 38824807299, 38830911279).
- Existing discriminators still green: gh-1532 preemption spike test, gh-1460 pause-proof arithmetic test, degenerate-flat rejection test (the guard stays meaningful under the min statistic).
- Full file: `dart test test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` → 10/10 passed; `dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings` clean; `dart format` clean.
- PR suites re-run: `dart test test/cli/cli_config_test.dart test/cli/stuck_tool_session_test.dart` → 140 passed.
- Full per-PR gate: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` → **11110 passed, 10 skipped (env-conditional), 0 failures**.
- Static gate parity: `dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings` → 0 issues in `lib/`/`test/`/`bin/` (the 78 reported issues are all `office_addin/dart`, the separate package the CI static job sets up explicitly before analyzing — `Static gates` passed on this head in run 38830911279).
- Post-merge-with-main parity: the head now also carries main's gh-1625 delta (`test/ci_release_*_guard_test.dart`) — `dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` → 32 passed.
- Fix is on `origin/ai/gh-1632` (commit `8712f7db2`, contained in branch head `5141afc65` after the automation's main-merge); CI re-validates the new head automatically.

## Scope note

AC5 (I4-REG orphan-`tool_stuck` ledger REG + red-blocks-merge CI) and AC6 (fa version in session header) remain open on gh-1632, as the PR description states — this PR intentionally does not claim them.

  `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time`, best doubling ratio **3.31x** vs the 3.2 bound (`2943 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped` in the shard).
- **Root cause — sustained runner contention, not a wrap regression.** The same assertion red on a second distinct head within one hour (run 38824807299, shard 0, ratio 3.35x), while the sibling absolute bounds (`1M cells < 100ms`, hard-cut) passed in the same shards. The growth harness already gated on the min ratio across 3 attempts (gh-1532), but each attempt still sampled each size with a **median of 5 timed runs**: a contention window spanning ≥3 of the doubled size's 5 runs in *every* attempt inflates every attempt median and the cross-attempt min cannot rescue it. That is exactly the observed shape — a sustained steal window on the shared `ubuntu-24.04-arm` pool, with the doubled (longer, 2× exposure) samples absorbing the preemptions and the small samples stable.
- This is a continuation of the known flake series on this assertion (#1530/#1531 → gh-1532 fix #1534; FLAKE-SYSTEMIC #1543). As with every prior round, the fix hardens the measurement; the 3.2 detection threshold (linear ≈ 2x, quadratic ≈ 4x+) is unchanged and no quarantine is applied — the guard stays live in the gate.
- Prior review findings re-verified at this head: the three stale dartdocs carry the gh-1632 I1 default; the PR body uses `Refs #1632` (no auto-close; AC5/AC6 stay open on the goal card); `git diff origin/main...HEAD` contains **zero** `apiKey` fixture-line changes in both test files.

## Approach

TDD, test-only change — production code untouched (`wrapAnsiLine` is proven correct by the passing absolute bounds):

1. **RED** — added a deterministic reproduction of the live failure shape using the file's `ContendedClock` (the gh-1532 precedent): 4 of the 5 doubled-size timed runs spiked with 30 ms of fake preemption in *each* of the 3 attempts (spike indices `{6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}` of the 30-call layout, layout-guarded like the existing preemption test). On the pre-fix harness this fails with ratio ~7x — median-of-5 takes a spiked value in every attempt — mirroring the live reds.
2. **GREEN** — `expectLinearGrowth` now samples each size with the new `minWrapMs` (fastest of the 5 timed runs) instead of the median. Contention can only ADD wall time, so the fastest observed run is the least-contaminated per-size estimate — the same principle gh-1532 applied across attempts, applied within them. A median needs a majority of clean runs; a min needs exactly one. A genuine quadratic regression inflates every doubled run including the fastest, so the guard keeps its detection margin (also pinned by the existing gh-1460 min-vs-median arithmetic test and the degenerate-flat rejection test, both still green).
3. Wall time is unchanged (same warm-up + 5 timed runs per size per attempt), so the shard duration budget is untouched.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `minWrapMs` helper; `expectLinearGrowth` switched median→min per size; new deterministic sustained-contention regression test; header/contract comments updated to the new statistic (no stale "median" claims left).
